- On August 20, 2023, Alaska Airlines Flight 1288, a Boeing 737-800 (N516AS), suffered substantial damage when its left main landing gear (MLG) collapsed after landing on wet Runway 20R at John Wayne Airport, California.
- The 112 occupants evacuated via airstairs onto a taxiway; no injuries, fire, explosion, or fuel leak occurred.
- The approach was conducted at night in instrument conditions, with rain, turbulence, shifting winds, and a recorded crosswind reaching 43 knots. Touchdown occurred at 2314:57 with approximately 1.71 G vertical acceleration.
- The crew initially observed all landing-gear indicators showing down and locked. After exiting the runway, the aircraft leaned about 5° left and rested on the left engine cowling; both engines were shut down.
- Examination found the left MLG aft trunnion pin fractured across its diameter. The fracture contained a fatigue “thumbnail” crack originating in an intergranular region beneath the chromium plating.
- Analysis indicated the crack developed over approximately 797 flight cycles after the landing gear’s 2018 overhaul and progressed until overstress failure during landing.
